newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica court sees serial killer's video confession.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica court sees serial killer's video confession.

text.p: A South African accused of one of the world's worst serial killings of recent times confessed to murdering 29 women in a video shown at his trial on Tuesday, national television said.

Moses Sithole, 32, is alleged to have strangled to death 38 women in and around the commercial heartland of Johannesburg in the last decade after luring them with the promise of work. He is also charged with 40 rapes.
He pleaded not guilty when his trial got under way in October but confessed to many of the killings in the bizarre tape shown in Pretoria Supreme Court.
He was filmed by a fellow inmate in jail to whom he had allegedly sold the rights to his life story. Prison authorities knew of the recording, state-run television news said.
Clips from the tape broadcast on the news showed Sithole calmly talking about how he had strangled victims.
"It takes a few minutes -- five minutes is too much," Sithole told his inmate interviewer, Charles Schoeman, who testified in court that Sithole's answers had been spontaneous.
TV news reported that the man accused of South Africa's worst serial sex killing had vigorously chewed gum in court as the tape was played, but showed no other signs of emotion.
It said that Sithole agreed to sell the rights of his story to Schoeman and another inmate after they pledged that part of the profit from it would go to his wife and children.
The defence did not contest the tape evidence. Sithole's trial was postponed until January 27.
